findings.issue: pw5's registration conjunct `(still == [respelled] or (respelled is None and os.name == "nt"))` drops the second-spelling check entirely when os.symlink fails on Windows (no privilege). On that platform pw5 then proves only the reaper's old forward-slash behaviour, so the Windows-only half of the fix (canonical comparison of a differently spelled tree) is covered by pw14's injected resolver alone and never by a real git listing. The default `_canonical_path` (realpath + normcase on a real nt) is likewise not exercised against a real 8.3 name by any case this task adds; the only evidence that realpath expands RUNNER~1 is the pw6 line in CI log 123039432291.log, read on the runner's Python.
findings.resolution: No code change needed for the product. Either make pw5 fail loudly (not silently narrow) when the link cannot be made on nt, or note in the case text which spelling was exercised; confirm on the next windows-latest run that pw5, pw6 and pw13 pass with the symlink branch actually taken.

preExisting.issue: _pool_tree identifies a pool tree by basename only (`prove-gates-pool-*` parent, `w<N>` leaf), anywhere on disk. A foreign worktree that happens to carry that shape and a dead or absent owner file is reaped (git worktree remove --force --force). Unchanged by this diff.
preExisting.resolution: Optionally also require the tree to sit under the pool parent (_pool_parent) before treating it as ours.

intent.note: Task clause: 'Fix the PRODUCT so every comparison of a worktree path, a pool root and an admin gitdir is made on one canonical spelling on Windows'. The diff adds _canonical_path (normcase(realpath)), routes _under through _worktrees.within_tree (separator-neutral boundary, so prefix-sharing siblings like pool-ab-other are not within pool-ab) and _drop_registration through the new _admin_of (_worktrees.same_tree on canonical spellings), and reap_stale groups pools by canonical key and returns realpath(root), the spelling open_workers records. Diagnosis checks out against the CI log: pw5, pw6 and pw13 fail on the single conjunct `reaped == [root as opened]` (log shows git's forward-slash spelling against the backslash root); the log does not show a live pool reaped (pw5 prints spared [] with 1 registered, which is the passing outcome), so the task text's 'live pool reaped' reading was a misreading and the executor's outcome says so correctly. pw13's 'not under the pool root' refusal is that case's expected refusal. Reaping condition is unchanged: `pid is None or alive(pid) is not False` still spares a missing, live or unknown owner (pw7 and pw5 cover them); nothing outside the pool can newly match, since _pool_tree is untouched and within_tree keeps the boundary. Task asked for 'POSIX-runnable cases that fail before the fix by injecting the Windows spellings ... and, for pid liveness, an injected probe': pw14 injects ntpath plus a short-to-long resolver, pw5 respells the registration through a symlink, pw15 uses the platform's real probe (pw5/pw7 keep the injected one). The task's suggested long-name expansion was not added; the executor argued realpath already expands 8.3 on the runner, supported by pw6's log line. The filed outcome describes the diff: only pool helpers and selftest hunks change. Not run on Windows in this review; the Windows CI leg is the final proof.

intent.inheritedTestsBasis: tests.gate is `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tools/prove-gates.py`, which selects tools/prove-gates.py's own --selftest. Read the pool cases in it: pw5 (spared only on explicit live, reaped only on False), pw6 and pw13 (foreign tree stays, by-name removal refuses outside the pool root, expectations are on the reaped list and registrations, not swallowed), pw7 (unknown pid spared), and the new pw14/pw15. None would pass with the reaper's dead-owner rule or the canonical comparison deleted: pw5 asserts reaped == [root] and 1 registered after the live probe; pw7 asserts spared == [] with a standing root; pw14 asserts the under/admin answers over spellings.
